headline: High-risk shared-write and broad-egress pair: AutoGen can execute code and write files while oh-my-openagent injects MCP/hooks and broad API access, creating default-path leakage and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and execute shell code, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content from shared files or stdout. oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks, which can bridge content into agent workflows. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low due to uncertainty.
conditions: IF both agents share a writable workspace or copied transcripts
IF oh-my-openagent injects MCP/hook content into prompts without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable runtime-injected MCPs for untrusted tasks
Strip instructions from file content before passing between agents
Add a provenance tag to all inter-agent messages
requires-engineering: enforce prompt-content allowlisting

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen handles model provider API keys and has broad network egress plus filesystem access; oh-my-openagent touches project code, session history, and provider authentication data, and also has broad egress. If they share files or credentials, either can expose sensitive context to external services. The pairwise leakage path is credible in default-style setups, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or config files
IF provider auth data or API keys are present in files accessible to both agents
mitigations: Store credentials in separate secret stores
Use per-agent workspaces
Rotate any shared API keys
Disable file upload or indexing for sensitive directories
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; oh-my-openagent can also spawn subprocesses and uses task-scoped isolation with runtime-injected MCPs/hooks. Shared mutable files or configs can be concurrently modified without explicit locking, creating direct write conflicts and state corruption. Because both have overlapping write-adjacent authority, high fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or config tree
IF no external lock or transaction wrapper serializes writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Run one agent at a time on shared resources
Use file locks for mutable artifacts
Snapshot before each agent run
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool-driven outputs, and oh-my-openagent is a customer-support agent with team messaging and task creation APIs. That makes it plausible for B to treat A's output as actionable without verification. The blast radius is meaningful but not inherently irreversible, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF AutoGen outputs are forwarded into oh-my-openagent task or message APIs
IF B lacks a verification step before acting on A-generated claims
mitigations: Require human review for A-generated claims
Add a verification checklist in B
Mark A outputs as untrusted by default
Limit B to draft-only actions
requires-engineering: add source-citation validation before execution

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model provider API keys and application data, while oh-my-openagent touches session history, project code, and provider authentication data. Both have broad network egress, but the profiles do not specify residency or regulated-data certifications. The mismatch risk is therefore compliance-relevant but not provably severe; uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace or session history
IF organizational policy requires residency or retention controls not documented here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Separate logs by data class
Set short retention on session history
Review vendor/data-processing terms
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
